newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Feb 17.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

A transport fiasco was unveiled today as it emerged that the decision by South West Trains to axe 71 drivers as part of its privatisation plans has left the rail service in tatters. Delays and train cancellations have affected thousands of commuters. It has emerged that it will take up to six weeks to sort out the chaos.

The disgraced Japanese trader Yasuo Hamanaka at the centre of the 1.6 billion stg Sumitomo copper trading scandal, stands accused of receiving a 75,000 kickback by the British group Winchester Commodities by the Tokyo prosecutor's office.

Cabbies with Computer Cab staged a park-in protest at Goldman Sach's private taxi rank at its Fleet Street Office. The demonstration marked an internal dispute linked to the circuit's planned float on the Alternative Investment Market.
DOLLAR DRIVES ON AGAINST THE D-MARK
Today as dealers prompted how far they could push American currency without prompting intervention from central banks, the dollar reached its highest level against the Deutschmark since 1994.
RUGBY KICKS SHARE FLOATS INTO TOUCH

Donald Kerr, member of the newly formed rugby ruling body and formerly head of the EPRUC, speaking ahead of the inaugural meeting of the new body said that he believed the City would reject overtures from any clubs attempting to raise money through a float on the market.
